prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” company that fits everyone — the right painter depends on your needs (home vs. condo vs. commercial), budget, timeline and the finishes you want. I can help you find the best match. A quick plan:

1) Quick questions so I can narrow it:
- Is this a residential or commercial job?
- Approx. size (number of rooms or square footage)?
- Do you want standard wall/ceiling paint only, or specialty finishes (trim, cabinetry, textured walls, wallpaper removal)?
- Preferred timeline or budget?

2) How to identify the best interior painter in St. Louis (check these criteria)
- Licensing & insurance (liability + workers’ comp)
- Strong recent reviews on Google, Yelp, Angi or Houzz
- Portfolio/photos of completed jobs in similar homes/styles
- Written, itemized estimate (labor, paint brand, number of coats, prep)
- Clear warranty/guarantee on workmanship and paint
- Good communication and a local office/phone number
- References you can call
- Clean-up and protection procedures for floors/furniture

3) Questions to ask any painter before hiring
- Are you licensed and insured? Can I see certificates?
- What brand and sheen of paint do you recommend?
- How many coats are included? Does the price include primer?
- How do you handle repairs (holes, trim, drywall)? Any extra charges?
- What is the projected start and completion date?
- What is your warranty and how do you handle punch-list items?

4) Pricing (ballpark)
- Smaller room: roughly $300–$800
- Whole-house interior (average 2,000 ft²): often $3,000–$8,000
- Per sq. ft. ranges commonly $1.50–$3.50 (depends heavily on prep, ceilings, trim)
These are rough; get 3 written quotes.

5) Next steps I can do for you
- If you want, tell me job details and I’ll suggest exactly what to ask for in estimates or draft a scope-of-work checklist you can give painters.
- If you paste or list a few local companies or links, I can compare reviews/quotes for you.

If you want, give the job details (type of rooms, square footage, any problem areas), and I’ll help you create a short-list and an estimate checklist to bring to painters.
